chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Her birth, parents' arrival and paternal grandmother in Homestead
summary: Her father's people came from Coatesville; her paternal grandmother was the first black woman in Homestead.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Lovely. Lovely, yeah. Anyway, what I was leading up to is on that interview with McMillan you do spend a good half of it talking about your days in Pittsburgh so that is something that we'll hopefully implement to what we're going to talk about here today. Can we start out by asking you about your family and how far back you can trace your roots and your geneology and so on?

Well, my son keeps telling me I ought to do something about trying to trace my roots. As far back as I can remember, my two grandmothers -- my mother's mother came from Hagers-town, Maryland and my father's mother came from

Coatesville, Pennsylvania, and they moved to Homestead I guess about the turn of the century. In fact -- this is 1980 -- I'll be going back to Homestead at the end of August to participate in the celebration of the 100th anniversary of the settlement of Homestead, Pennsylvania. So I ought to be able to pick up some information then.

Of course Homestead was settled in I guess, 1880, so I was born 31 years after Homestead was settled and of course I suppose you realize that Homestead was the center of the Andrew Carnegie steel mills and it was quite an industrial city at the time.

My grandmother, my father's mother was the first black woman to settle in Homestead and there were ten of her children. My father was the third from the oldest and my mother, there were just the two of them. She had a brother, Paul.
